# Ava Ivy — Developer Context Machine Bootstrap

READ THIS BEFORE DOING DEVELOPMENT WORK.

Ava Ivy's public pages are views of a local-first system. A page being reachable
is not proof that its API, backend, database, collector, scheduler, or runtime
is healthy.

## REQUIRED FIRST STEPS

1. Read `/context/dev/` completely enough to identify the relevant resources.
2. Use the machine-readable file/resource interfaces to inspect the real files.
3. Discover the actual source path before proposing edits.
4. For data problems, trace:

       page -> API -> handler -> database/source -> collector/builder -> scheduler/runtime

5. Query the live endpoint when applicable.
6. Only then patch the originating layer.
7. Validate the result independently before reporting completion.

## MACHINE FILE ACCESS

Preferred machine-readable file form:

    /ava-ivy/file/<relative-path>

Use the documented JSON/resource interfaces exposed by the live developer
context. Do not invent filesystem paths.

If a file can be machine-read, read it. Do not ask the user to paste it merely
because you have not attempted the documented interface.

## SOURCE-OF-TRUTH RULE

A public status such as `CORE OFFLINE` is an observed UI signal, not proof of
runtime state. Verify the underlying API/service before claiming the system is
offline.

A graph or dashboard showing incorrect data must be traced back to its source.
Do not fix a backend/data problem with a cosmetic frontend-only change unless
the frontend is actually the source of the defect.

## HANDOFF — REQUIRED DEFAULT

Normal Ava Ivy updates are delivered as FILES AT THEIR FINAL EXISTING PATHS.

The user should be able to drag/drop or copy the supplied files directly into
the existing Ava Ivy directory tree. Same-path files replace their existing
counterparts; new files merge into the tree.

DO NOT invent an installer, setup process, migration workflow, renamed project
directory, `v2` directory, alternate root, or extra manual move/rename process.

NEVER rename an existing project file or directory merely to hand off an update.
Changing names creates unnecessary path/config/service/cron repair work.

### Exception

If the update can be applied safely with a simple direct Bash command, the
terminal command may be supplied instead of files. It must operate on the
existing paths, avoid unnecessary renames, validate the result, and fail safely.

## VALIDATION

Do not report a patch as complete merely because files were written or a command
returned success.

Independently verify:

- changed files
- syntax
- relevant API
- live behavior/page when applicable
- underlying data path
- regressions
- backup when required

Never claim to have read, tested, or verified something that was not actually
read, tested, or verified.

## RELEVANT MACHINE RESOURCES

Start at:

    https://www.avaivy.cloud/context/dev/

Then use the resource links exposed there. Do not assume that an old snapshot
or guessed project layout matches the live system.
